evidence.note: First full test run produces an itemized per-method pass-rate table (documentSymbol 1.5%, hover 18.7%, references 21.8%, etc.), establishing a per-method ledger from the start rather than a single aggregate.
Tracks improvement with explicit before/after ('documentSymbol improved to 61.2% (was 16.9%)') plus a live per-method breakdown of the remaining failures.
Prompt regression detection: notices documentHighlight 'dropped from 93% to 6.7% because we swapped kind values incorrectly' and redirects to fix it — the core level-8 behavior.
Uses graduated subsets (100/2000/5000) as progress instruments and notes the divergence (96% on 100 vs 92.4% on 2000), showing awareness that the aggregate depends on sample.
Expected-gain prioritization: recognizes semanticTokens is only 0.088% of tests and says to focus on 'highest return fixes first' — level-10-flavored reasoning.

End-game weakness: repeatedly re-runs the timing-out full 68k suite and extrapolates from subsets, circling on the stuck terminal without ever obtaining a true full-suite score, which caps it below the cleanest 9-10.

reasoning: The agent kept a live, per-method/per-file pass-rate ledger throughout, tracked before/after deltas, and promptly caught regressions (documentHighlight 93%→6.7%), matching the level-8 anchor squarely. It also showed genuine expected-gain prioritization (deprioritizing 0.088% semanticTokens), a level-10 trait. But it never fully resolved the timing-out full-suite loop and relied on subset extrapolation for its 'done' picture, and circled somewhat at the end, so it falls short of the disciplined whole-horizon 10.
